lane_argv_targeting.target_title: Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
lane_argv_targeting.jd_text:
Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD
lane_argv_targeting.briefing_text:
# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD | Reports to Partnerships (partner GTM context) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s partner opportunity is not simply distribution. Enterprise deployment requires partners to translate a rapidly evolving AI product surface into governed workflows, measurable use cases, and repeatable implementation patterns.

The operating tension is scale versus control: expand enterprise adoption through outside delivery capacity without losing technical quality, customer trust, product feedback fidelity, or Anthropic’s safety posture. This role likely sits at
the point where partner strategy becomes deployable architecture and field execution.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is a product- and platform-led AI company organized around Claude, with a public-benefit-corporation identity and a stated focus on reliable, interpretable, and steerable systems.

Its commercial model is increasingly enterprise-oriented: Claude serves business teams and developers, while enterprise offerings emphasize security, compliance, and administration. The company wins through model capability and trust, but
enterprise value is realized through workflow integration, change management, and production adoption.

The central operating challenge is converting a frontier-AI product into repeatable, partner-deliverable customer outcomes while preserving a coherent technical and safety standard across a growing ecosystem.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic is building a broad Claude business across direct product use, enterprise deployments, developer access, and cloud, technology, and services partners. That creates a more complex operating model than a direct-sales AI assistant
business.

Enterprise adoption is not framed solely as access provisioning. Anthropic’s deployment guidance covers technical setup, change management and launch, signaling that adoption quality, governance, and organizational rollout are part of the
value realization motion.

As partner routes expand, decision rights become important: Product and Engineering need high-signal field feedback; commercial teams need repeatable solutions; partners need enough technical clarity and enablement to deliver independently.
The key pressure is standardizing where possible without constraining high-value industry and customer-specific work.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The critical stakeholder map spans Partnerships, enterprise commercial leadership, Product, Engineering, developer-facing teams, security and trust functions, and customer-adoption teams.

External stakeholders are likely to include cloud, technology, and services-partner executives; partner solution and delivery leaders; and enterprise technical buyers responsible for security, architecture, data, and business adoption.

For this role, influence matters as much as formal authority. The most valuable internal contribution is likely turning field patterns into shared technical assets, clear escalation paths, and product feedback that can be acted on.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is positioned for complex problem solving, data analysis, coding, and knowledge work. Anthropic’s enterprise product framing combines business-team use with developer use, making architecture conversations broader than model
selection or API access.

Claude for Enterprise includes an administrator-led deployment model and explicitly addresses security, compliance, technical setup, and launch. This creates a practical architecture agenda around identity and access, data handling,
governance, integration design, enablement, and operational rollout.

Anthropic’s stated emphasis on reliability, interpretability, and steerability is a commercial design constraint as well as a research orientation. Partner-built solutions need to make those properties legible to enterprise technical and
risk stakeholders.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly organizes its ecosystem across cloud, technology, and services partners. This is a hybrid motion: partners can extend reach and implementation capacity, while Anthropic must remain technically involved enough to protect
solution quality and accelerate learning.

Accenture has publicly positioned its Anthropic relationship around enterprise AI deployment, productivity, and new-product creation. That indicates the ecosystem is aimed at client delivery and transformation work, not only referral or
resale.

The partner motion creates a need for reusable reference architectures, partner training, technical validation, joint solution development, and well-defined escalation. Strong ecosystem execution should reduce one-off solutioning while
giving partners credible ownership of customer outcomes.

## Recent Events & Urgency
In 2026, Anthropic announced a $100 million commitment to the Claude Partner Network, including partner enablement infrastructure such as training materials, sales playbooks, and a partner portal. The investment signals a deliberate move to
operationalize enterprise partner capacity rather than rely only on opportunistic alliances.

The urgency is executional: ecosystem investment raises the bar for partner readiness, field consistency, and measurable deployment outcomes. It also increases the importance of translating recurring partner friction into improvements in
technical assets, enablement, and product roadmap decisions.

Competitive pressure in enterprise AI is likely to favor vendors that can pair capable models with secure deployment, credible services capacity, and repeatable business-use-case adoption.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise AI architecture that connects model capabilities to governed production workflows.
- Partner enablement designed for repeatable customer delivery, not one-off technical support.
- Joint solution development with cloud, technology, and services ecosystems.
- Technical leadership across commercial, product, engineering, and partner-delivery stakeholders.
- Reference architectures, implementation playbooks, and feedback loops that improve field velocity.
- Security, compliance, adoption, and change-management considerations in AI deployments.
- Coaching technical teams through ambiguity while raising technical consistency and customer outcomes.
- Balancing rapid commercial expansion with responsible-AI and trust requirements.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic is investing in partner infrastructure at a moment when enterprise AI success depends on deployment quality, not just model access.
- The interesting operating problem is scaling partner-led adoption while keeping technical standards and safety expectations consistent.
- Claude Enterprise’s deployment model suggests that architecture, governance, and change management are central to customer value realization.
- Anthropic’s ecosystem spans cloud, technology, and services partners, creating a meaningful intersection of solution design and partner enablement.
- The role appears relevant to someone who can turn field learning into reusable partner assets and actionable product feedback.
- Anthropic’s public-benefit and reliability orientation gives enterprise technical conversations a trust-and-governance dimension beyond standard GTM execution.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, leadership scope, technical depth, and partnership outcomes must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
